label: GitHub

value.text: Leave unchecked — the gateway uses the authorization-code flow.

steps: Open GitHub → Settings → Developer settings → OAuth Apps → New OAuth App (link below).
Fill the fields with the values above.
Click Register application, then copy the Client ID.
Click Generate a new client secret and copy it — GitHub shows it only once.
Paste both into Client ID and Client Secret below, then Save.

label: GitLab

value.text: Keep checked — the gateway holds the secret server-side.
Select the scopes the MCP server documents (see Suggested scopes below).

steps: Open GitLab → User Settings → Applications (link below) and add a new application.
Fill the fields with the values above and pick the scopes.
Save application, then copy the Application ID and Secret.
Paste them into Client ID and Client Secret below, then Save.

label: Google

value.text: Not required for the gateway — leave empty.

steps: Open Google Cloud Console → APIs & Services → Credentials (link below).
Create Credentials → OAuth client ID → Web application.
Add the redirect URI above under Authorized redirect URIs, then Create.
Copy the Client ID and Client Secret into the fields below, then Save.

label: Atlassian (Jira / Confluence)
steps: Open the Atlassian developer console (link below) and create an OAuth 2.0 (3LO) app.
Under Authorization, set the Callback URL to the value above.
Under Settings, copy the Client ID and Secret.
Paste them into Client ID and Client Secret below, then Save.

label: Slack
steps: Open Slack → Your Apps (link below) and create a new app.
Under OAuth & Permissions, add the Redirect URL above and the scopes the MCP server needs.
From Basic Information, copy the Client ID and Client Secret.
Paste them into Client ID and Client Secret below, then Save.

label: Notion
steps: Open Notion → My integrations (link below) and create a new integration.
Set it to a Public integration and add the Redirect URI above.
Copy the OAuth client ID and client secret.
Paste them into Client ID and Client Secret below, then Save.

label: Linear
steps: Open Linear → Settings → API → Applications (link below) and create an application.
Add the Callback URL above.
Copy the Client ID and Client Secret.
Paste them into Client ID and Client Secret below, then Save.

label: Asana
steps: Open Asana → My apps (link below) and create a new app.
Under OAuth, add the Redirect URL above.
Copy the Client ID and Client Secret.
Paste them into Client ID and Client Secret below, then Save.

label: Airtable
steps: Open Airtable → Developer hub → OAuth integrations (link below) and register an integration.
Set the OAuth redirect URL to the value above and select the scopes.
Copy the Client ID and generate a Client Secret.
Paste them into Client ID and Client Secret below, then Save.

label: Other / generic provider

fields.label: Application / client name
fields.hint: Any name — identifies the gateway, not a user.

fields.label: Redirect / callback URL
fields.hint: The one field that must match exactly.

value.text: Authorization Code — enable PKCE / S256 if the provider offers it.

steps: Open your provider’s developer console and create a new OAuth application (a confidential/server-side app, not a public/native one).
Fill the app’s fields with the values above — the callback URL must match character-for-character.
Save the app, then copy the issued Client ID and generate a Client Secret.
Paste both into Client ID and Client Secret below, then Save.
